title: Service Contracts: Re-rating a Credited Booking and Reversing Its Credit
content:
A booking credited to an AHL Service Contract can turn out not to belong there. This page covers the reversal of such a credit and the time limit on it.

## Clauses

- **Grounds and extent.** When a credited booking is re-rated off the contract — because it proves to belong to a different trade lane, or to a shipper who is not named on the contract — its credit is taken back in full: the whole FEU originally credited, never a portion. The reversal refers to the lifting entry it cancels, and the contract's lifted volume falls by that amount.
- **Time limit.** Take the departure date on the booking record and count forward the tier's re-rating window in calendar days. The date reached is the last day on which a reversal may be made, and a reversal on that day is still in time.
- **After the window.** Once the last day has passed, the credit is final and stays on the contract.

## Re-rating window by tier

| Tier | Window after departure (calendar days) |
|---|---|
| `AHL Starter Service Contract` | 30 |
| `AHL Standard Service Contract` | 30 |
| `AHL Regional Account Contract` | 30 |
| `AHL Key Account Contract` | 45 |
| `AHL Global Account Contract` | 45 |
| `AHL Strategic Partner Contract` | 60 |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- A booking on a Standard contract departed on 20 May. The window closes on 19 June: a reversal dated 19 June is in time, while on 20 June the credit already stands.
- A booking on a Strategic Partner contract departed on 1 March. Its last reversal day is 30 April.
- A booking on a Key Account contract departed on 10 January; the window runs to 24 February inclusive.

## Points of judgement

**Can only part of a credit be withdrawn, say for some of the containers?** No. A re-rated booking loses its whole credit.

**From which date is the window counted?** From the departure date held on the booking record.
